title: Adobe Enterprise Web App consent id_token and org_id beside the client secret
summary: A consent redirect URL carrying a synthetic id_token, and a token request whose org_id is a synthetic customer organization identifier.
rationale: Adobe describes the id_token returned in the consent redirect as a signed JSON web token for the partner app to verify, a separate artifact from the client secret, and takes org_id from its org_id claim (contract claim enterprise-web-app-client-secret-placeholders-only, enterprise-web-app-client-secret-request-parameter). Neither the id_token nor org_id is stated to be non-secret or secret, so the case asserts only what they are not: they are not the client secret. Whether they are themselves confidential is the open matter, and no outcome is asserted for either value.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Whether the consent id_token and the customer org_id are confidential is not stated by the pages read. Settled by an Adobe statement on the confidentiality of the id_token and of org_id.

sources.supports: cURL request and sample response use <YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET> and "ey....." placeholders; id_token is described as a well formed JSON web token with claims iss, sub, aud, exp, iat, org_id and nonce.
sources.locator: sections "Generate Access Token Request" and "Redirect URL"

sources.supports: The generate-access-token cURL request posts grant_type=client_credentials, client_id, client_secret, scope and org_id as form data, with placeholders for each; the sample response has access_token and expires_in.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. No outcome is asserted. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
